articles.title: FTC Catches 'Pharma Bro' Shkreli Secretly Trading 60+ Drug Stocks Despite Lifetime Industry Ban
articles.summary: Martin Shkreli, banned for life from the pharmaceutical industry after his fraud conviction, allegedly traded stocks in at least 60 drug companies in direct violation of federal court orders. The FTC and seven states are now seeking contempt findings and forfeiture of trading profits. This case exposes how pharma insiders treat regulatory bans as suggestions — and how long enforcement takes when the industry's own are involved.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Failures From Investors — SEC Now Circling
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet insulin delivery device, triggering a 37% stock collapse and a securities fraud class action. The company's FDA compliance issues were apparently concealed from the public while insiders continued to tout the product. When medical devices fail patients and the truth gets buried to protect share prices, the harm is doubled.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment Under Fire: Mental Illness Is Not Consent Revocation
articles.summary: A Reason investigation challenges the legal and ethical framework that allows governments to forcibly medicate psychiatric patients who explicitly refuse treatment. The piece names the core contradiction: if informed consent is medicine's bedrock principle, psychiatric patients are being systematically stripped of that right based on diagnosis alone. This is the uncomfortable conversation mainstream psychiatry refuses to have.

articles.title: Ensign Group Buried Patient Neglect, Faked Staffing Data, and Billed Feds Anyway — Now Facing Fraud Suit
articles.summary: Ensign Group, one of the largest nursing home operators in the country, is accused of concealing systemic patient neglect, manipulating quality and staffing metrics reported to regulators, running an administrator-license rental scheme, and submitting improper billing to federal programs. The stock dropped 8% when the truth began leaking out — meaning investors got the warning patients never did. This is institutional elder care fraud with a federal billing dimension.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Hit With Federal Fraud Complaint — FTC Says Company Deceived Patients and Investors Alike
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, accusing the telehealth giant of deceptive practices that misled both patients and investors. A securities class action has followed, with the lead plaintiff deadline set for November 2026. The case raises urgent questions about how DTC telehealth platforms market compounded and off-label drugs to vulnerable patients with inadequate informed consent.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Rewrite Their Own Genome to Escape Treatment — And Oncologists Are Just Now Catching Up
articles.summary: A sweeping analysis of nearly half a million cells from pancreatic tumor patients reveals that cancer cells don't just mutate at diagnosis — they continuously reshape their genetic architecture to evade every treatment thrown at them. This challenges the static tumor model that underpins most chemotherapy protocols and explains why pancreatic cancer remains a near-certain death sentence. The question the oncology establishment must answer: how long has this been known, and why hasn't the treatment paradigm shifted?

articles.title: Live Vaccines Given to 220 Immunocompromised IBD Patients Caused Zero Infections — So Why Is the Warning Still Gospel?
articles.summary: A real-world study of 220 IBD patients on immunosuppressive biologics who accidentally received live vaccines — including MMR and varicella — found zero cases of measles, mumps, or chickenpox. The blanket contraindication against live vaccines in immunocompromised patients has denied protection to millions, yet this data point is being treated as a footnote rather than a call to revisit official guidance. When the evidence contradicts the dogma, the dogma wins — until it doesn't.

articles.title: GDF15 Deficiency Silently Starves the Fetus — And Nobody Is Talking About What's Suppressing This Protein
articles.summary: New research published in PLOS Biology confirms that placenta-specific GDF15 is essential for fetal growth, with deficiency triggering growth restriction by collapsing the fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 signaling axis. Circulating GDF15 levels drop in at-risk pregnancies, yet this biomarker is not part of standard prenatal screening. With miscarriage and fetal growth restriction rates climbing, the failure to act on emerging placental biology is a clinical negligence story hiding in plain sight.

articles.title: Shkreli Defies Lifetime Pharma Ban — FTC Says He Traded 60+ Drug Stocks Anyway
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states are moving to hold Martin Shkreli in contempt after alleging he traded stocks in at least 60 pharmaceutical companies in direct violation of a court-ordered lifetime ban. Shkreli, convicted of securities fraud in 2017, appears to have treated his ban as a suggestion rather than a legal boundary. Regulators are demanding disgorgement of profits and surrender of all pharma holdings.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Failures From Investors — Stock Craters 37%

Real-world evidence keeps vindicating what official guidance refuses to update.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer's Shape-Shifting Cells Are Outsmarting Every Drug We Throw at Them
articles.summary: Analysis of nearly half a million cells across dozens of pancreatic tumor patients reveals that cancer cells are continuously and dynamically rewriting their own genetic code, enabling them to evade treatment in real time. This fundamentally challenges the static tumor model that has driven oncology drug development for decades. The implications for why so many late-stage cancer trials fail — and why the industry keeps running them anyway — are damning.

articles.title: GDF15 Deficiency Drives Fetal Growth Restriction — What Does This Mean for Pregnancy Interventions?
articles.summary: New research shows that placenta-specific GDF15 is essential for fetal growth, operating through the fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 axis — and that low circulating levels are linked to fetal growth restriction in clinical studies. This mechanistic pathway has been largely overlooked by obstetric research priorities dominated by pharmaceutical intervention targets. Understanding what suppresses GDF15 in human pregnancy — including drugs, environmental exposures, and nutritional deficiencies — is a question the system has not been eager to fund.

articles.title: Early-Life Antibiotics Wreck Gut Immunity — Fecal Transplants Show What Drugs Won't Fix
articles.summary: New mouse research confirms that early antibiotic exposure causes lasting intestinal immune dysregulation via the TLR4/MyD88 signaling pathway — and that fecal microbiota transplantation from adult donors can reverse it. The pediatric overprescription of antibiotics has been documented for decades, yet standard of care has barely changed. This study is further evidence that the microbiome destruction we inflict on children has immunological consequences the pharmaceutical industry has no pill to solve.

Understanding what the placenta is actually doing biochemically could transform how we prevent fetal growth restriction — if anyone is listening.
